$comment: Committed regression baseline for the detection-coverage gate (suggested enhancement, docs/plan/26-09-12-tasks-red-blue-agentic-posture.md — 'fail a build when a newly confirmed finding lands on a route with no telemetry'). Mirrors corpus/baseline.json's and corpus/blue-team-baseline.json's shape and conventions exactly. The scorer (`pnpm --filter @montr/qa qa:detection-coverage`) exits non-zero when a real run's `gapRate` exceeds `gapRateMax`. `gapRate` is built ONLY from A7's tri-state DetectionCoverage.detected === false (a GENUINE, unambiguous telemetry gap — the route was resolved, analyzed for logging, and either has no logging call at all or has logging with no detection rule covering it) — `detected === "unknown"` (ambiguous: route unresolved, route never analyzed, or console-only logging with no structured fields) is deliberately EXCLUDED from this threshold and only ever reported as an informational rate, mirroring the blue-team-corpus gate's discipline of never letting ambiguity masquerade as a real regression signal. Tighten (never loosen) as telemetry/detection-rule coverage improves.
$measurement: Measured 2026-09-12 against the REAL apps/worker L0-L3 pipeline (real L0 App Map, real semgrep + gitleaks L1 discovery, real L2 correlation, real L3 static confirmation — FAKE in-process LLM gateway only) run via `node scripts/detection-coverage-scan.mjs --out detection-coverage-scan.json` over the same 16-repo golden corpus `scripts/corpus-scan.mjs` scores, reading back the REAL, PERSISTED DetectionCoverage rows A7's `persistDetectionCoverageForScan` (apps/worker/src/runners.ts's Layer 3 runner) writes for every confirmed finding — never a hand-computed verdict. Measured result: 16 confirmed findings across 6 repos with at least one confirmed finding (vulnerable-nextjs, dvna, javaseccode, jvm-vuln, pygoat, python-vuln) produced 16 DetectionCoverage rows: detectedFalse=10, detectedUnknown=6, detectedTrue=0 — gapRate=62.5%, unknownRate=37.5%, coverageRate=0.0%. This is the REAL, currently-measured state of the pipeline, NOT an aspirational target: detectedTrue is honestly 0 because nothing in the L0-L3 pipeline this driver exercises generates a DetectionRule for these findings (B3's generateDetectionRules is invoked from packages/report's report-builder / the blue-team-corpus harness, not from the Layer 3 confirmation runner this gate scans) — every confirmed finding that resolves a route and has telemetry to evaluate therefore reads as detectedFalse (a route was found, has no covering rule) rather than detectedTrue, exactly per evaluateCoverageForFinding's own documented branches (packages/appmap/src/coverage-analysis.ts). gapRateMax below sits a real safety margin (12.5 percentage points) above the measured 62.5% so the gate passes honestly today and breaks on a genuine regression (e.g. a route losing its logging call, or App Map route resolution breaking) from here. minConfirmedFindings sits a small safety margin (10) below the measured 16 to catch an empty/degraded corpus run (e.g. semgrep/gitleaks missing) without being so tight that ordinary corpus variance trips it.
$statisticalCaveat: 16 confirmed findings is a small sample — one additional detectedFalse verdict would move gapRate from 62.5% to roughly 68.75%, still under gapRateMax below, but the margin is real, not huge. Because detectedTrue is currently 0 across the whole corpus (no DetectionRule is generated during L0-L3 for any of these findings), this gate cannot yet distinguish 'newly ungenerated a detection rule' from 'always had no rule' — it only catches a NEW loss of logging/telemetry (a detectedFalse verdict flipping from a previously detectedUnknown or, once detectionRuleId generation is wired into this path, detectedTrue verdict) or a route-resolution regression. Read gapRate together with unknownRate (37.5%) — a large unknown share means a meaningful fraction of this measurement is genuinely ambiguous, not a clean floor; treat both as directional until the corpus and the detection-rule-generation call path this driver exercises both grow (see corpus/README.md's equivalent golden-corpus caveat for the same reasoning).
